sentences.text:
This is the second bail application moved by the applicant for release on bail in Sessions Trial No.
174 of 2022 (State vs. Shivmurat Pasi), arising out of Case Crime No. 189 of 2022, under Sections 376(3), 313, 511, 504, 506 IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Charwa, District Kaushambi.

2. The only ground urged in support of the present application is that the applicant has been in judicial custody for the last three years, and yet the trial has not been concluded, though it is stated to be at its fag end.
3. Learned A.G.A., while opposing the prayer for bail, submits that this being the second bail application, there is no fresh ground disclosed in the present application.
It is contended that the grounds now raised were already considered by this Court at the time of rejection of the first bail application.
It is further submitted that the plea of prolonged incarceration, in the absence of any substantial change in circumstance, cannot be treated as a fresh ground for grant of bail.

Reliance has been placed on various pronouncements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court wherein it has been held that successive bail applications can be entertained only upon emergence of new circumstances or events, and that mere long detention in custody does not by itself constitute a change in circumstance warranting reconsideration of bail in cases involving grave and heinous offences.

4. Having considered the rival submissions and upon perusal of the record, it is evident that the first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court after due consideration of all materials available on record.
The present application does not disclose any fresh ground which has arisen subsequent to such rejection.

The contentions advanced on behalf of the applicant relating to appreciation of evidence or credibility of witnesses pertain to matters within the domain of trial and cannot be adjudicated at this stage.

5. As regards the plea of long incarceration, it is well settled that the same, in isolation, cannot constitute a fresh ground for grant of bail in offences of such serious and sensitive nature,
particularly where the allegations involve rape of a minor girl and her consequent pregnancy,
punishable under Section 376(3) IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act.

6. In view of the gravity of the offence, the absence of any fresh or new ground, and the settled legal position governing successive bail applications, this Court finds no justification to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the second bail application stands dismissed.
